note.backdrop: Tuesday closed as a rotation: QQQ -1.99%, SPY -0.49%, while the Dow fund rose 0.79% and small caps 0.53% (StockTitan). Chips fell hard (in the bank's bars: Micron -11.0%, AMD -8.9%, Intel -8.1%, Nvidia -5.9%, Analog Devices -17.4%, HPE -16.3%, Dell -11.8%), while retailers (Abercrombie +19.7%, Kohl's +19.5%, Dick's +14.6%, Dollar Tree +11.2%) and drug makers (Cogent +17.4%, Kymera +15.7%, Disc Medicine +15.3%, Insmed +14.1%, Lilly +3.2%) rose. After the close the reports are mixed to weak: Ambarella -37.6%, Urban Outfitters -12.1%, Workday -7.2%, Nutanix -7.9%; Dell +0.9%. The after-hours market is quiet (SPY -0.3%). The case file's futures (-1.0%) and gold (-2.9%) lines likely compare with Monday's close, not Tuesday's: the known stale baseline.

read.says: Nov 24 close: QQQ -1.99%, SPY -0.49%, DIA +0.79%, IWM +0.53%; Micron -11.01%, Nvidia -5.86%, HPE -16.31% (below its Friday close); Insmed +14.13%, Embecta +40.64%, Shoe Station -18.39%. After hours: Ambarella -37.55% on fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $70-75 million against $115.2 million in the third, its CEO citing rising memory prices leading customers to cut outlooks; Dell +4.35% at 6:02 p.m. on record revenue of $54.9 billion and an AI backlog of $132.3 billion, slightly higher by 7:59; Urban Outfitters -12.71% on record sales; Nutanix and Workday down more than 7%; HP +2.00%.

themes.beneath: Ambarella -37.6% after hours is -36.7% of its own; in the bank's bars it had already closed -20.0% in Tuesday's session, before its report, with chips. Its partners barely moved after hours (Ceva 0.0%, Alpha and Omega -0.4%, Rambus -1.1%), so tonight the read stays with Ambarella (the pond). Dell's record revenue and $132.3 billion backlog held it up (+0.9%) after its -11.8% day: the demand side remains strong; the question is margins (inferred).
themes.cause: Ambarella guided fourth-quarter revenue to $70-75 million against a record $115.2 million in the third quarter and a Street view near $112.6 million; its CEO said rising memory prices and shortages are leading many customers to cut their outlooks (StockTitan; s1, s2).
themes.mechanism: Memory is a cost to everyone who builds devices and servers on top of it: HPE guided AI server margins lower on component costs on Monday night, a Dell preview flagged rising memory costs, and now Ambarella's customers buy fewer of its chips because memory makes their products dearer.

themes.beneath: The pattern of the week: results above expectations, growth guided slower, the stock lower (HPE, Semtech, Workday, Nutanix). Workday's stock has fallen more than 16% this year (s9). FactSet -6.8% after hours sits in the cluster but no story names it.
themes.cause: Workday beat and raised its fiscal 2027 subscription revenue and margin forecasts (revenue +11.2%, subscription +12.8%, AI products' annual recurring revenue above $750 million, up over 130%), but guided fourth-quarter subscription growth down to 10% and said its third-quarter backlog was helped by early renewals. Nutanix beat on earnings ($0.73 against $0.60) and raised its cash-flow guidance, but its annual recurring revenue of $2.63 billion was a little under the $2.65 billion expected.
themes.mechanism: Each fell on its own report (Workday -7.2%, Nutanix -7.9%); their partners Salesforce (-0.4%), ServiceNow (-0.6%) and Adobe (-0.1%) barely moved after hours. Autodesk -3.6% moved against a small wave of +0.3 from its neighbours.
